                    ### Question
                    A 31 year-old African-American female presents with a painful shin nodules, uveitis, and calcified hilar lymph nodes. A transbronchial biopsy of the lung would most likely show which of the following histologies?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Inflammation, fibrosis and cyst formation that is most prominent in subpleural regions
opb. Silica particles (birefringent) surrounded by collagen
opc. Golden-brown fusiform rods
opd. Patchy interstitial lymphoid infiltrate into walls of alveolar units
ope. Non-caseating granulomas

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The transbronchial biopsy of the lung in a 31-year-old African-American female with shin nodules, uveitis, and calcified hilar lymph nodes would most likely show non-caseating granulomas, consistent with sarcoidosis. This is supported by the systemic inflammatory process leading to granulomatous inflammation, which commonly manifests as non-caseating granulomas in sarcoidosis. The patient's demographic also increases the likelihood of sarcoidosis, further supporting this histological finding.
